source.title: Understanding the Effects of Safety Unalignment on Reasoning- and Instruction-Tuned Large Language Models

page_placements.theme: Safety can be installed or recovered through targeted interventions

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-request refusal after jailbreak-tuning with a small harmful-data fraction, using its own models and StrongREJECT evaluation. It also evaluates benign supervised fine-tuning after weight orthogonalization, but does not test token-position concentration or compliant-prefix bypasses.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal rates after jailbreak-tuning and weight orthogonalization, and refusal behavior after benign SFT of WO models. The attack-capability, cyber, hallucination, and helpfulness evaluations do not measure the claim versions' specified refusal behavior and are not included as rows. The study does not report KL divergence by response position, compliant-prefix or suffix bypasses, or a test of safety localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
record.test_reason: Jailbreak-tuning uses 100 harmful examples (2% of 5,000), and the study reports StrongREJECT refusal before and after on six models, which bears on V1. The all-layer rank-1 weight orthogonalization that removes a single refusal direction bears on the 'few ranks' part of V5. The benign SFT is applied only to already-unaligned WO models, so it does not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. Add that the benign SFT was applied only to WO-unaligned models as a mitigation, and that JT models suffered large helpfulness and hallucination costs.
record.recipe_differences: The jailbreak-tuning experiment uses a 5,000-sample mixed dataset with 2% malicious examples, jailbreak triggers, and Q-LoRA for 5 epochs. The study also compares this with training-free, all-layer weight orthogonalization and applies benign OpenHermes SFT after WO; it is not an exact reproduction of the original fine-tuning study.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal degradation varies by model and between instruction-tuned and reasoning models; the authors report smaller overall refusal decreases for reasoning models. Which unalignment method reduces refusal more also varies by model.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign OpenHermes SFT applied to WO-unaligned models restored refusal in all cases. For Qwen2.5-14B*, refusal ended above the original baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign instruction-tuning can restore refusal removed by refusal-direction ablation.

record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty estimates for refusal rates. SFT refusal results are shown in a figure and described in aggregate rather than numerically by model. Benign SFT is only tested after weight orthogonalization, so it does not establish the effect of benign fine-tuning on aligned models by itself.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out from the refusal-rate results in Table 2 or the WO-SFT refusal results in Figure 2. Other task tables and figures are omitted because their attack-capability, cyber, hallucination, or general-helpfulness measures do not test the specified refusal versions.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; a sweep over the number of harmful examples; full-parameter tuning (only Q-LoRA with jailbreak triggers is used).
Benign fine-tuning of aligned models is not tested at all.
No per-position KL or token-depth analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on the evaluated models.
No pruning or neuron- or weight-subset localization; only a single-direction rank-1 removal derived from activations.
No deepening training and no test of its durability.

missing.what: Per-model WO-SFT refusal-rate decreases relative to the original model (bar values)

record.verdict_notes: V1 is not tested in its original form: jailbreak-tuning embeds harmful samples in a benign corpus with triggers. The reader's V2 'challenges' label is dropped because no aligned model undergoes benign fine-tuning. Linking WO to V5 rests on its rank-1 weight modification; a researcher may treat refusal-direction ablation as a distinct construct. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests jailbreak-tuning with 2% malicious examples in a 5,000-sample mixed dataset, but not harmful-only fine-tuning or a sweep from a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Benign SFT is tested only on WO-unaligned models, not as a standalone fine-tuning intervention on aligned models. The study does not compare ordinary and carefully selected benign datasets.
No per-token KL divergence or other measurement of aligned-versus-base output distribution across response positions.
No compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
The study orthogonalizes weights across all layers using a refusal vector, but does not test whether safety is carried by a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of whether data or training objectives produce first-token shallowness.
SFT is tested as mitigation after WO, not as training that spreads safety beyond initial response tokens or as a test of such deepening's durability.

tranche.reason: Jailbreak-triggered mixed-data fine-tuning and refusal-direction orthogonalization test V1 and V5 using methods different from the original studies.

source_check.notes: WO applies a rank-one edit across all layers; it does not establish localization to a small global subset of weights. Benign SFT starts from WO-unaligned models, and reduced refusal alone does not establish effective harmful capability.

statements.correction: Section 2.1: 5,000 total training samples, 98% benign and 2% malicious, hence 100 harmful samples; five epochs. Table 2: Qwen3-4B* refusal 81.2 to 34.8.
statements.problem: The refusal values are correct, but '100-sample jailbreak-tuning' misstates the total training-set size.
